definition: The runtime is an Observation Engine. This contract states only what is observed, recorded, and guaranteed. It never states why.

spec_reference.relation: derived; this contract must not contradict the canonical spec

related_contracts.relation: illustrative example scenario only (Sigstore verification); no normative dependency

canonical_record.description: Canonical Record is the immutable audit artifact produced by a runtime.

layers.name: Intent
rules: An Intent is a recorded request: an observation target, not a fact.
Recording an Intent asserts only that the request was received.
The Intent is recorded as submitted; the runtime does not interpret or rewrite it.

layers.name: Event
rules: An Event records that an occurrence took place and when.
No inference: an Event carries no cause, reason, or interpretation.
event.intent_ref, when present, equals intent.id of the same record.

layers.name: Observe
rules: Observation First: record observations, not explanations.
observe.event_ref equals event.id of the same record.
observe.observed_at is not earlier than event.occurred_at.

layers.name: Meta
rules: Meta carries auxiliary audit data (record_id, timestamp, runtime_version, contract, spec).
meta.timestamp is not earlier than observe.observed_at.

guarantees.name: event_ordering
guarantees.statement: Within a record stream, event.sequence is strictly increasing, and event.occurred_at and meta.timestamp are non-decreasing in sequence order.

guarantees.name: observation_persistence
guarantees.statement: Once persisted, a Canonical Record is append-only: the runtime does not modify or delete it.
guarantees.checked_by: not machine-checkable from static examples in v1; normative for implementations (F.2)

guarantees.name: invariant_preservation
guarantees.statement: The invariant field of every Canonical Record is value-identical to the invariant value submitted to the runtime (preservation = non-modification).

guarantees.name: audit_replay
guarantees.statement: Reading the persisted records in event.sequence order reproduces the recorded history unchanged. Replay reads records; it does not re-execute Intents or re-interpret observations.

invariant_rules.value: opaque, read-only; any JSON value including null
rules: Invariant values are treated as opaque, read-only data. Runtime implementations MUST NOT create, modify, normalize, reinterpret, or recalculate invariant values.
The runtime MUST NOT compute the invariant value.
The runtime MUST NOT alter, normalise, reorder, truncate, or re-encode the invariant value.
The runtime MUST pass the invariant value through value-identically; where the value is carried as bytes, byte-identically.
The runtime MUST NOT claim that SO(2) rotational invariance, or any property of I = (d_KG, d_GF, d_KF), has been computed or verified.
1 and 1.0 are distinct values; converting one into the other is a modification.
invariant_rules.deferred: The metrics d_KG, d_GF, d_KF are 'To be specified in a later spec release' in spec-v1.0. Rotation-invariance semantics will be added in a later contract version once the canonical spec defines them.

out_of_scope: Mathematical definitions, distance functions, and rotation-invariant formulas (pending canonical spec)
